ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Josephine Baker — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Baker returns for a preventive visit, eight weeks after her twelve-week review. She finished cardiac rehabilitation in the summer and has been rehearsing four mornings a week without chest pain or breathlessness; she plans to sing and dance in a short run of concerts this autumn. The nosebleed in June has not come back. She has not had a mammogram or a colon test for many years and asks what she is due for. She takes all her medicines from a weekly pill box. Her finances remain strained but she has a contract for the autumn concerts. [S]

Follow-up: Mammogram and DXA booked; FIT kit to return by mail; hepatitis C and HIV tests drawn today; optometry. Seven-month review in five weeks with RSV, zoster and Tdap vaccines. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1969-10-20: seven-month review: antiplatelet plan to twelve months, blood pressure, kidney function, angina status and plans for the year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. After the heart attack she wanted her wishes written down. She named a longtime friend as her health care agent, and the form was completed and copied into the chart. She wants full treatment, including resuscitation, for any illness she might recover from, and she wants her children cared for if she is ill. If she had a severe stroke or other illness with little chance of recovering her ability to speak, move and recognize the people she loves, she would not want long-term life support and would want to be kept comfortable. She will tell her agent and her family. [S]
